<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/ProcessingSystem/PipeRoller.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessConvertible + IProcessIdentity (OreSystem C — interface), OrePiecePoolManager (OreSystem C — concrete for spawn),
//       BuildingManager (FREE — light materials)

/// <summary>
/// I roll two plates into a pipe. Two-stage process: first plate enters → Process1 animation,
/// second plate enters → Process2 animation → weld two plates into pipe → spawn pipe at output.
/// If plates are different resource types → produce SlagPipe. If non-plate ore enters → jammed.
/// Non-plate ore with PipePrefab → direct ConvertToPipe. Jammed ore periodically launched upward.
/// SkinnedMeshRenderers show plate visuals during animation. Weld particle plays on creation.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building, conveyor feeds plates into trigger.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Processing/PipeRoller")]
public class PipeRoller : MonoBehaviour
{
	#region Inspector Fields
	[SerializeField] Animator _animator;
	[SerializeField] Transform _plate1Transform;
	[SerializeField] Transform _plate2Transform;
	[SerializeField] Transform _pipeTransform;
	[SerializeField] Transform _outputTransform;
	[SerializeField] List<ParticleSystem> _jammedParticles;
	[SerializeField] float _launchJammedObjectCooldown = 1f;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundDefinition _launchJammedObjectSound, _process1Sound, _createPipeSound;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundPlayer _processSoundPlayer;
	[SerializeField] GameObject _slagPipePrefab;
	[SerializeField] SkinnedMeshRenderer _lightMeshRenderer;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] LoopingSoundPlayer _jammedLoopingAudioSource;
	[SerializeField] SkinnedMeshRenderer _plate1Renderer, _plate1PolishedRenderer;
	[SerializeField] SkinnedMeshRenderer _plate2Renderer, _plate2PolishedRenderer;
	[SerializeField] ParticleSystem _weldParticle, _slagWeldParticle;
	#endregion

	#region Private State
	float lastLaunchTime;
	bool isJammed;
	List<IProcessConvertible> waitingList = new List<IProcessConvertible>();
	HashSet<Component> jammedOre = new HashSet<Component>();
	bool isProcessing;
	AnimationClip firstPlateClip, secondPlateClip;
	ResourceType firstResourceType;
	bool firstIsPolished;
	GameObject firstPipePrefab;
	#endregion

	void OnEnable()
	{
		RefreshJammedEffects();
		// → cache animation clip lengths
		if (_animator != null)
		{
			firstPlateClip = _animator.runtimeAnimatorController.animationClips.FirstOrDefault(c => c.name == "PipeRoller_Process1");
			secondPlateClip = _animator.runtimeAnimatorController.animationClips.FirstOrDefault(c => c.name == "PipeRoller_Process2");
		}
		_plate1Renderer.enabled = false; _plate1PolishedRenderer.enabled = false;
		_plate2Renderer.enabled = false; _plate2PolishedRenderer.enabled = false;
	}

	/// <summary> Each frame: check jam state, periodically launch jammed ore. </summary>
	void Update()
	{
		bool wasJammed = isJammed;
		isJammed = jammedOre.Count > 0;
		if (isJammed != wasJammed) { RefreshJammedEffects(); lastLaunchTime = Time.time; }
		if (isJammed && Time.time - lastLaunchTime > _launchJammedObjectCooldown)
		{
			lastLaunchTime = Time.time;
			if (Random.value < 0.5f) StartCoroutine(WaitThenLaunchJammed());
		}
	}

	IEnumerator WaitThenLaunchJammed()
	{
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(0.3f);
		if (jammedOre.Count == 0) yield break;
		Component jammed = jammedOre.ElementAt(Random.Range(0, jammedOre.Count));
		if (jammed == null) yield break;
		Rigidbody rb = jammed.GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
		if (rb != null) { Vector3 dir = Vector3.up * 2f + -transform.forward + Random.insideUnitSphere * 0.2f; rb.AddForce(dir * 2f, ForceMode.Impulse); rb.AddTorque(dir * 6f, ForceMode.Impulse); }
	}

	void RefreshJammedEffects()
	{
		foreach (var ps in _jammedParticles) { var em = ps.emission; em.enabled = isJammed; }
		ChangeLightMaterial(isJammed ? Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.OrangeLightMaterial : Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.GreenLightMaterial);
	}

	void ChangeLightMaterial(Material mat) { var mats = _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials; mats[1] = mat; _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials = mats; }

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		IProcessIdentity identity = other.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
		if (conv == null || identity == null) return;
		if (identity.GetPieceType() == PieceType.plate && conv.GetPipePrefab() != null)
		{
			if (!isProcessing)
			{
				isProcessing = true;
				if (firstResourceType == ResourceType.INVALID) StartCoroutine(ProcessFirstPlate(conv, identity));
				else StartCoroutine(CreatePipe(conv, identity));
			}
			else waitingList.Add(conv);
		}
		else if (conv.GetPipePrefab() != null) conv.ConvertToPipe();
		else jammedOre.Add(other.GetComponent<Component>());
	}

	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		if (conv != null) waitingList.Remove(conv);
		jammedOre.Remove(other.GetComponent<Component>());
	}

	/// <summary> Stage 1: store first plate's info via IProcessConvertible + IProcessIdentity. </summary>
	IEnumerator ProcessFirstPlate(IProcessConvertible conv, IProcessIdentity identity = null)
	{
		_plate2Renderer.enabled = false; _plate2PolishedRenderer.enabled = false;
		if (conv == null) { isProcessing = false; yield break; }
		if (identity == null) identity = (conv as Component)?.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
		firstResourceType = identity?.GetResourceType() ?? ResourceType.INVALID;
		firstIsPolished = identity != null && identity.GetPolishedPercent() >= 1f;
		firstPipePrefab = conv.GetPipePrefab();
		_plate1Renderer.enabled = !firstIsPolished; _plate1PolishedRenderer.enabled = firstIsPolished;
		Material mat = (conv as Component)?.GetComponent<Renderer>()?.sharedMaterial;
		if (firstIsPolished) _plate1PolishedRenderer.sharedMaterial = mat;
		else _plate1Renderer.sharedMaterial = mat;
		identity?.Delete();
		isProcessing = true;
		if (_animator != null) _animator.Play("PipeRoller_Process1", -1, 0f);
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(firstPlateClip != null ? firstPlateClip.length * 0.95f : 2f);
		isProcessing = false;
		if (waitingList.Count > 0) { var next = waitingList[0]; waitingList.RemoveAt(0); StartCoroutine(CreatePipe(next)); }
	}

	/// <summary> Stage 2: combine two plates → pipe. Types differ → slag. Via IProcessConvertible + IProcessIdentity. </summary>
	IEnumerator CreatePipe(IProcessConvertible conv, IProcessIdentity identity = null)
	{
		if (conv == null) { firstResourceType = ResourceType.INVALID; isProcessing = false; yield break; }
		if (identity == null) identity = (conv as Component)?.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
		bool ore2Polished = identity != null && identity.GetPolishedPercent() >= 1f;
		// → determine output prefab
		GameObject selectedPrefab = _slagPipePrefab;
		if (identity != null && firstResourceType == identity.GetResourceType())
			selectedPrefab = (firstIsPolished == ore2Polished) ? conv.GetPipePrefab() : (firstIsPolished ? conv.GetPipePrefab() : firstPipePrefab);
		_plate2Renderer.enabled = !ore2Polished; _plate2PolishedRenderer.enabled = ore2Polished;
		Material mat = (conv as Component)?.GetComponent<Renderer>()?.sharedMaterial;
		if (ore2Polished) _plate2PolishedRenderer.sharedMaterial = mat;
		else _plate2Renderer.sharedMaterial = mat;
		identity?.Delete();
		isProcessing = true;
		if (_animator != null) _animator.Play("PipeRoller_Process2", -1, 0f);
		float clipLen = secondPlateClip != null ? secondPlateClip.length : 3f;
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(clipLen * 0.52f);
		_plate1Renderer.enabled = false; _plate1PolishedRenderer.enabled = false;
		_plate2Renderer.enabled = false; _plate2PolishedRenderer.enabled = false;
		// → spawn pipe via IPoolSpawner
		GameObject pipeGO = PoolSpawnerBridge.Spawner?.SpawnPooled(selectedPrefab, _pipeTransform.position, Quaternion.identity);
		if (selectedPrefab == _slagPipePrefab) _slagWeldParticle.Play(); else _weldParticle.Play();
		Rigidbody pipeRb = pipeGO?.GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
		Collider pipeCol = pipeGO?.GetComponent<Collider>();
		if (pipeGO != null)
		{
			if (pipeRb != null) pipeRb.isKinematic = true;
			if (pipeCol != null) pipeCol.enabled = false;
			pipeGO.tag = "Untagged";
			pipeGO.transform.parent = _pipeTransform; pipeGO.transform.localPosition = Vector3.zero; pipeGO.transform.localRotation = Quaternion.identity;
		}
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(clipLen * 0.2f);
		if (pipeGO != null)
		{
			if (pipeRb != null) pipeRb.isKinematic = false;
			if (pipeCol != null) pipeCol.enabled = true;
			pipeGO.transform.parent = null; pipeGO.transform.position = _outputTransform.position; pipeGO.transform.rotation = _outputTransform.rotation;
			pipeGO.tag = "Grabbable";
		}
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(clipLen * 0.24f);
		firstResourceType = ResourceType.INVALID;
		isProcessing = false;
		if (waitingList.Count > 0) { var next = waitingList[0]; waitingList.RemoveAt(0); StartCoroutine(ProcessFirstPlate(next)); }
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/ProcessingSystem/PolishingMachine.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessProgressable + IProcessIdentity (OreSystem C — interface), ConveyorBelt (ConveyorSystem D — ChangeSpeed), BuildingManager (FREE)

/// <summary>
/// I gradually polish ore pieces. While ore is in my trigger, I call OrePiece.AddPolish(delta) each frame.
/// If a dirty ore piece enters (MakesPolishingMachineDirty), I become dirty: slow down conveyor,
/// change brush/machine materials to dirty variants, wait _timeToStayDirty seconds to auto-clean.
/// Animator plays polishing or dirty animation based on state.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building, ore rides on built-in conveyor belt through the brushes.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Processing/PolishingMachine")]
public class PolishingMachine : MonoBehaviour
{
	[SerializeField] Animator _polishingAnimator;
	[SerializeField] float _polishingTime = 1.75f;
	[SerializeField] float _timeToStayDirty = 10f;
	[SerializeField] float _standardConveyorSpeed;
	[SerializeField] float _dirtyConveyorSpeed;
	[SerializeField] ConveyorBelt _conveyor;
	[SerializeField] List<Renderer> _brushRenderersToMakeDirty;
	[SerializeField] Material _cleanMachineMaterial;
	[SerializeField] Material _dirtyMachineMaterial;
	[SerializeField] Material _cleanBrushMaterial;
	[SerializeField] Material _dirtyBrushMaterial;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _lightMeshRenderer;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] LoopingSoundPlayer _dirtySoundPlayer;

	bool isDirty;
	List<IProcessProgressable> polishingList = new List<IProcessProgressable>();
	float timeUntilClean;

	void OnEnable() => MakeClean();

	/// <summary> Each frame: polish all ore in trigger. If any is dirty → MakeDirty. Auto-clean after timer. </summary>
	void Update()
	{
		polishingList.RemoveAll(item => item == null || !(item as UnityEngine.Component).isActiveAndEnabled);
		// → check if any ore makes machine dirty (via IProcessIdentity)
		foreach (var prog in polishingList)
		{
			var identity = (prog as UnityEngine.Component)?.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
			if (identity != null && identity.GetMakesDirty()) { MakeDirty(); break; }
			if (!isDirty) prog.AddPolish(Time.deltaTime / _polishingTime);
		}
		if (isDirty)
		{
			_polishingAnimator.SetBool("IsPolishing", false);
			_polishingAnimator.SetBool("IsDirty", true);
			timeUntilClean -= Time.deltaTime;
			if (timeUntilClean <= 0f) MakeClean();
		}
		else
		{
			_polishingAnimator.SetBool("IsPolishing", polishingList.Count > 0);
		}
	}

	/// <summary> Sets dirty state — changes materials, slows conveyor, resets timer. </summary>
	void MakeDirty()
	{
		timeUntilClean = _timeToStayDirty;
		if (isDirty) return;
		isDirty = true;
		// → swap brush materials to dirty
		foreach (var r in _brushRenderersToMakeDirty)
		{
			var mats = r.sharedMaterials;
			mats[0] = _dirtyBrushMaterial; mats[1] = _dirtyMachineMaterial;
			r.sharedMaterials = mats;
		}
		ChangeMachineMaterial(_dirtyMachineMaterial);
		ChangeLightMaterial(Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.OrangeLightMaterial);
		_conveyor.ChangeSpeed(_dirtyConveyorSpeed);
		// Phase H: _dirtySoundPlayer.Play();
	}

	/// <summary> Restores clean state — clean materials, normal speed. </summary>
	void MakeClean()
	{
		isDirty = false;
		foreach (var r in _brushRenderersToMakeDirty)
		{
			var mats = r.sharedMaterials;
			mats[0] = _cleanBrushMaterial; mats[1] = _cleanMachineMaterial;
			r.sharedMaterials = mats;
		}
		ChangeMachineMaterial(_cleanMachineMaterial);
		ChangeLightMaterial(Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.GreenLightMaterial);
		_conveyor.ChangeSpeed(_standardConveyorSpeed);
		_polishingAnimator.SetBool("IsDirty", false);
		// Phase H: _dirtySoundPlayer.Stop();
	}

	void ChangeMachineMaterial(Material mat)
	{
		var mats = _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials; mats[0] = mat; _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials = mats;
	}
	void ChangeLightMaterial(Material mat)
	{
		var mats = _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials; mats[2] = mat; _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials = mats;
	}

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessProgressable prog = other.GetComponentInParent<IProcessProgressable>();
		if (prog != null) polishingList.Add(prog);
	}
	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessProgressable prog = other.GetComponentInParent<IProcessProgressable>();
		if (prog != null) polishingList.Remove(prog);
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/ProcessingSystem/RodExtruder.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessConvertible (OreSystem C — interface only). ZERO concrete OrePiece import.
// Note: ConvertToRod() returns GameObject — we activate it at output. Renderer/MeshFilter accessed via GetComponent on the GO.

/// <summary>
/// I extrude ingots into rods. When an ingot (OrePiece with RodPrefab) enters trigger:
/// ConvertToRod → hide rod GO → show rod renderer at start position → lerp to output position
/// over ProcessingTime → hide renderer → show rod GO at output. Dual processing lanes
/// (_isProcessing1/_isProcessing2) allow 2 rods to extrude simultaneously with minimum spacing.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building, conveyor feeds ingots into trigger.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Processing/RodExtruder")]
public class RodExtruder : MonoBehaviour
{
	#region Inspector Fields
	[SerializeField] Transform _outputTransform;
	[SerializeField] float _processingTime = 1.5f;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundDefinition _extrudeRodSound;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundPlayer _processRodSoundPlayer;
	[SerializeField] Transform _rodStartTransform;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _rodRenderer1;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _rodRenderer2;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _lightRenderer;
	#endregion

	#region Private State
	List<IProcessConvertible> waitingList = new List<IProcessConvertible>();
	bool isProcessing1, isProcessing2;
	MeshFilter rodMeshFilter1, rodMeshFilter2;
	float timeSinceProcessed = 999f;
	#endregion

	void Awake()
	{
		rodMeshFilter1 = _rodRenderer1.GetComponent<MeshFilter>();
		rodMeshFilter2 = _rodRenderer2.GetComponent<MeshFilter>();
	}

	void OnEnable()
	{
		_rodRenderer1.enabled = false; _rodRenderer2.enabled = false;
		_rodRenderer1.transform.localPosition = _rodStartTransform.localPosition;
		_rodRenderer2.transform.localPosition = _rodStartTransform.localPosition;
	}

	bool IsAvailable() => !isProcessing1 || !isProcessing2;

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		if (conv != null && conv.GetRodPrefab() != null)
		{
			if (IsAvailable()) StartCoroutine(ExtrudeRod(conv));
			else waitingList.Add(conv);
		}
	}

	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		if (conv != null) waitingList.Remove(conv);
	}

	void Update() => timeSinceProcessed += Time.deltaTime;

	/// <summary> Convert to rod via interface → hide → lerp renderer start→end → show rod at output. Dual lane. </summary>
	IEnumerator ExtrudeRod(IProcessConvertible conv)
	{
		GameObject rodGO = conv.ConvertToRod();
		bool usingLane1 = !isProcessing1;
		if (rodGO == null) yield break;
		rodGO.SetActive(false);
		if (usingLane1) isProcessing1 = true; else isProcessing2 = true;
		// → wait for minimum spacing between rods
		float minTime = _processingTime * 0.75f;
		while (timeSinceProcessed < minTime) yield return null;
		timeSinceProcessed = 0f;
		// → setup renderer
		Renderer selRenderer = usingLane1 ? _rodRenderer1 : _rodRenderer2;
		MeshFilter selMF = usingLane1 ? rodMeshFilter1 : rodMeshFilter2;
		selRenderer.sharedMaterial = rodGO.GetComponent<Renderer>().sharedMaterial;
		selMF.sharedMesh = rodGO.GetComponent<MeshFilter>().sharedMesh;
		selRenderer.transform.position = _rodStartTransform.position;
		selRenderer.enabled = true;
		// Phase H: _processRodSoundPlayer.PlaySound(_extrudeRodSound);
		// → lerp from start to output
		float elapsed = 0f;
		Vector3 startPos = _rodStartTransform.position, endPos = _outputTransform.position;
		while (elapsed < _processingTime)
		{
			elapsed += Time.deltaTime;
			selRenderer.transform.position = Vector3.Lerp(startPos, endPos, elapsed / _processingTime);
			yield return null;
		}
		selRenderer.enabled = false;
		// → show rod at output
		if (rodGO != null) { rodGO.transform.position = _outputTransform.position; rodGO.transform.rotation = _outputTransform.rotation; rodGO.SetActive(true); }
		if (usingLane1) isProcessing1 = false; else isProcessing2 = false;
		// → process next
		if (waitingList.Count > 0) { var next = waitingList[0]; waitingList.RemoveAt(0); StartCoroutine(ExtrudeRod(next)); }
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/ProcessingSystem/RollingMill.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessIdentity + IProcessConvertible (OreSystem C — interface), IPoolSpawner (owned — interface for spawn),
//       BuildingManager (FREE — light materials). ZERO concrete imports.

/// <summary>
/// I flatten ingots into plates. When an ingot (OrePiece with PlatePrefab) enters my trigger,
/// I play the rolling animation, show a plate visual, wait ProcessingTime, then spawn the plate
/// prefab at OutputTransform. If a non-plate-eligible ore enters → it's jammed: smoke particles,
/// orange light, periodically launched upward with random force. Waiting list queues extra ingots.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building, conveyor feeds ingots into trigger.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Processing/RollingMill")]
public class RollingMill : MonoBehaviour
{
	#region Inspector Fields
	[SerializeField] Animator _rollingAnimator;
	[SerializeField] float _processingTime = 3f;
	[SerializeField] Transform _plateTransform;
	[SerializeField] Transform _outputTransform;
	[SerializeField] List<ParticleSystem> _jammedParticles;
	[SerializeField] float _launchJammedObjectCooldown = 1f;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundDefinition _launchJammedObjectSound;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundDefinition _processPlateSound;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundPlayer _processPlateSoundPlayer;
	[SerializeField] MeshRenderer _lightMeshRenderer;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] LoopingSoundPlayer _jammedLoopingAudioSource;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _plateRenderer;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _platePolishedRenderer;
	#endregion

	#region Private State
	float lastLaunchTime;
	bool isJammed;
	List<IProcessConvertible> waitingList = new List<IProcessConvertible>();
	HashSet<Component> jammedOre = new HashSet<Component>();
	bool isProcessing;
	#endregion

	void OnEnable()
	{
		if (_plateRenderer != null) _plateRenderer.enabled = false;
		if (_platePolishedRenderer != null) _platePolishedRenderer.enabled = false;
		RefreshJammedEffects();
	}

	/// <summary> Each frame: check jam state, periodically launch jammed ore upward. </summary>
	void Update()
	{
		bool wasJammed = isJammed;
		isJammed = jammedOre.Count > 0;
		if (isJammed != wasJammed) { RefreshJammedEffects(); lastLaunchTime = Time.time; }
		if (isJammed && Time.time - lastLaunchTime > _launchJammedObjectCooldown)
		{
			lastLaunchTime = Time.time;
			if (Random.value < 0.5f) StartCoroutine(WaitThenLaunchJammed());
		}
	}

	IEnumerator WaitThenLaunchJammed()
	{
		// Phase H: SoundManager.PlaySoundAtLocation(_launchJammedObjectSound, transform.position);
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(0.3f);
		if (jammedOre.Count == 0) yield break;
		Component jammed = jammedOre.ElementAt(Random.Range(0, jammedOre.Count));
		if (jammed == null) yield break;
		Rigidbody rb = jammed.GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
		if (rb != null)
		{
			Vector3 dir = Vector3.up + -transform.forward + Random.insideUnitSphere * 0.2f;
			rb.AddForce(dir * 2f, ForceMode.Impulse);
			rb.AddTorque(dir * 6f, ForceMode.Impulse);
		}
	}

	void RefreshJammedEffects()
	{
		foreach (var ps in _jammedParticles)
		{
			var em = ps.emission; em.enabled = isJammed;
			ChangeLightMaterial(isJammed ? Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.OrangeLightMaterial : Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.GreenLightMaterial);
			// Phase H: _jammedLoopingAudioSource.Toggle(isJammed);
		}
	}

	void ChangeLightMaterial(Material mat)
	{
		var mats = _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials; mats[3] = mat; _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials = mats;
	}

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		if (conv != null && conv.GetPlatePrefab() != null)
		{
			if (!isProcessing) { isProcessing = true; StartCoroutine(PressIngot(conv, other)); }
			else waitingList.Add(conv);
		}
		else if (other.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>() != null)
		{
			// → not plate-eligible → jammed
			jammedOre.Add(other.GetComponent<Component>());
		}
	}

	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		if (conv != null) waitingList.Remove(conv);
		jammedOre.Remove(other.GetComponent<Component>());
	}

	/// <summary> Called by external clear-all to reset state. </summary>
	public void OnAllOreCleared() { jammedOre.Clear(); waitingList.Clear(); }

	/// <summary> Shows plate visual, plays animation, waits, spawns plate at output. Via IProcessConvertible + IProcessIdentity. </summary>
	IEnumerator PressIngot(IProcessConvertible conv, Collider triggerCol = null)
	{
		var identity = (conv as Component)?.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
		GameObject platePrefab = conv.GetPlatePrefab();
		if (platePrefab != null && platePrefab.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>() != null)
		{
			// → pool-spawn path: show plate visual, animate, spawn pooled ore
			bool isPolished = identity != null && identity.GetIsPolished();
			// → set plate renderer material from the plate prefab's renderer
			Material plateMat = platePrefab.GetComponent<Renderer>()?.sharedMaterial;
			if (isPolished && _platePolishedRenderer != null) _platePolishedRenderer.sharedMaterial = plateMat;
			else if (_plateRenderer != null) _plateRenderer.sharedMaterial = plateMat;
			if (_plateRenderer != null) _plateRenderer.enabled = !isPolished;
			if (_platePolishedRenderer != null) _platePolishedRenderer.enabled = isPolished;
			identity?.Delete();
			// Phase H: _processPlateSoundPlayer.PlaySound(_processPlateSound);
			isProcessing = true;
			if (_rollingAnimator != null)
			{
				_rollingAnimator.speed = 1f / _processingTime;
				_rollingAnimator.Play("RollingMill_Process", -1, 0f);
			}
			yield return new WaitForSeconds(_processingTime * 0.9f);
			if (_plateRenderer != null) _plateRenderer.enabled = false;
			if (_platePolishedRenderer != null) _platePolishedRenderer.enabled = false;
			// → spawn plate at output via IPoolSpawner
			PoolSpawnerBridge.Spawner?.SpawnPooled(platePrefab, _outputTransform.position, _outputTransform.rotation);
		}
		else
		{
			// → direct conversion path
			conv.ConvertToPlate();
		}
		isProcessing = false;
		if (waitingList.Count > 0) { var next = waitingList[0]; waitingList.RemoveAt(0); StartCoroutine(PressIngot(next)); }
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/ProcessingSystem/ShakerTable.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessProgressable (OreSystem C — interface only). ZERO concrete OrePiece import.

/// <summary>
/// I gradually sieve ore pieces. While ore is in my trigger, I call IProcessProgressable.AddSieveValue(delta)
/// each frame. After SievingTime seconds total, the ore completes sieving (converts to sieved variant).
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building, ore sits on shaker belt (ConveyorBeltShaker variant).
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Processing/ShakerTable")]
public class ShakerTable : MonoBehaviour
{
	[SerializeField] float _sievingTime = 6f;

	List<IProcessProgressable> sievingList = new List<IProcessProgressable>();

	/// <summary> Each frame: add sieve progress to all ore in trigger. Clean nulls. </summary>
	void Update()
	{
		sievingList.RemoveAll(item => item == null || !(item as UnityEngine.Component).isActiveAndEnabled);
		foreach (var ore in sievingList)
			ore.AddSieveValue(Time.deltaTime / _sievingTime);
	}

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessProgressable prog = other.GetComponentInParent<IProcessProgressable>();
		if (prog != null) sievingList.Add(prog);
	}

	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessProgressable prog = other.GetComponentInParent<IProcessProgressable>();
		if (prog != null) sievingList.Remove(prog);
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/ProcessingSystem/ThreadingLathe.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessConvertible (OreSystem C — interface only). ZERO concrete OrePiece import.

/// <summary>
/// I thread rods into threaded rods. When a rod (OrePiece with RodPrefab) enters trigger:
/// ConvertToThreaded → hide rod GO → show rod renderer → play ThreadingLathe_Process animation
/// → at 1.5s move renderer to spinning parent → at 2.25s swap to threaded material/mesh →
/// at 5.5s move back to regular parent → at 8s hide renderer + show rod GO at output.
/// Multi-stage animation with parent swapping for spin visual.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building, conveyor feeds rods into trigger.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Processing/ThreadingLathe")]
public class ThreadingLathe : MonoBehaviour
{
	#region Inspector Fields
	[SerializeField] Transform _outputTransform;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundDefinition _threadRodSound;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundPlayer _processRodSoundPlayer;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _rodRenderer;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _dummyWholePartRenderer;
	[SerializeField] Renderer _lightRenderer;
	[SerializeField] Animator _animator;
	[SerializeField] Transform _rodRegularParent;
	[SerializeField] Transform _rodSpinningParent;
	#endregion

	#region Private State
	List<IProcessConvertible> waitingList = new List<IProcessConvertible>();
	bool isProcessing;
	MeshFilter rodMeshFilter, dummyMeshFilter;
	#endregion

	void Awake()
	{
		rodMeshFilter = _rodRenderer.GetComponent<MeshFilter>();
		dummyMeshFilter = _dummyWholePartRenderer.GetComponent<MeshFilter>();
		_rodRenderer.enabled = false;
	}

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		if (conv != null && conv.GetRodPrefab() != null)
		{
			if (!isProcessing) { isProcessing = true; StartCoroutine(ThreadRod(conv)); }
			else waitingList.Add(conv);
		}
	}

	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessConvertible conv = other.GetComponent<IProcessConvertible>();
		if (conv != null) waitingList.Remove(conv);
	}

	/// <summary> Multi-stage threading: convert → show renderer → animate → parent swap → show at output. </summary>
	IEnumerator ThreadRod(IProcessConvertible conv)
	{
		var comp = conv as UnityEngine.Component;
		Material origMat = comp?.GetComponent<Renderer>()?.sharedMaterial;
		Mesh origMesh = comp?.GetComponent<MeshFilter>()?.sharedMesh;
		GameObject rodGO = conv.ConvertToThreaded();
		if (rodGO == null) { isProcessing = false; yield break; }
		rodGO.SetActive(false);
		// Phase H: _processRodSoundPlayer.PlaySound(_threadRodSound);
		isProcessing = true;
		// → show rod with original material
		_rodRenderer.sharedMaterial = origMat; rodMeshFilter.sharedMesh = origMesh;
		_rodRenderer.enabled = true;
		_dummyWholePartRenderer.sharedMaterial = origMat; dummyMeshFilter.sharedMesh = origMesh;
		_animator.Play("ThreadingLathe_Process");
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(1.5f);
		// → move to spinning parent for rotation visual
		_rodRenderer.transform.SetParent(_rodSpinningParent);
		_rodRenderer.transform.localPosition = Vector3.zero;
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(0.75f);
		// → swap to threaded material/mesh
		_rodRenderer.sharedMaterial = rodGO.GetComponent<Renderer>().sharedMaterial;
		rodMeshFilter.sharedMesh = rodGO.GetComponent<MeshFilter>().sharedMesh;
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(3.25f);
		// → move back to regular parent
		_rodRenderer.transform.SetParent(_rodRegularParent);
		_rodRenderer.transform.localPosition = Vector3.zero;
		_rodRenderer.transform.localRotation = Quaternion.identity;
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(2.5f);
		// → hide renderer, show rod at output
		_rodRenderer.enabled = false;
		if (rodGO != null) { rodGO.transform.position = _outputTransform.position; rodGO.transform.rotation = _outputTransform.rotation; rodGO.SetActive(true); }
		yield return new WaitForSeconds(1.1f);
		isProcessing = false;
		if (waitingList.Count > 0) { var next = waitingList[0]; waitingList.RemoveAt(0); StartCoroutine(ThreadRod(next)); }
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/BaseBasket.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IBasketTrackable (OreSystem C — interface only). ZERO concrete OrePiece import.

/// <summary>
/// I'm a trigger zone that tracks which processable objects are inside me. SorterFilterBasket extends.
/// Uses IBasketTrackable for bidirectional tracking — AddBasketRef/RemoveBasketRef instead of
/// directly writing to OrePiece.BasketsThisIsInside. IMagnetGrabbable.IsInBasket() still works
/// because OrePiece implements both IBasketTrackable and IMagnetGrabbable.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as child of sorter buildings. SorterFilterBasket extends for filter logic.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Sorting/BaseBasket")]
public class BaseBasket : MonoBehaviour
{
	protected List<IBasketTrackable> _basketOreList = new List<IBasketTrackable>();

	protected virtual void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IBasketTrackable trackable = other.GetComponentInParent<IBasketTrackable>();
		if (trackable != null && !_basketOreList.Contains(trackable))
		{
			_basketOreList.Add(trackable);
			trackable.AddBasketRef(this);
		}
	}

	protected virtual void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IBasketTrackable trackable = other.GetComponentInParent<IBasketTrackable>();
		if (trackable != null) { _basketOreList.Remove(trackable); trackable.RemoveBasketRef(this); }
	}

	protected virtual void OnDisable()
	{
		foreach (var trackable in _basketOreList) trackable.RemoveBasketRef(this);
		_basketOreList.Clear();
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/BulkSorter.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessIdentity (OreSystem C — interface), SorterFilterBasket (same system), UtilsPhaseB (FREE). ZERO concrete OrePiece import.

/// <summary>
/// I sort ore into 3 lanes: Left, Right, Straight — based on two SorterFilterBaskets.
/// Ore enters trigger → if matches Left filter → enable left colliders only (ignore center+right).
/// If matches Right → enable right only. If matches both → random pick. Else → straight (center).
/// Uses Physics.IgnoreCollision to steer ore by enabling/disabling lane colliders per ore piece.
/// Also ignores collisions between ore going different directions to prevent jams.
/// Re-sorts on enable (domain reload safe). Subscribes to DebugManager.ClearedAllPhysicsOrePieces.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building. Two SorterFilterBaskets define left/right criteria.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Sorting/BulkSorter")]
public class BulkSorter : MonoBehaviour
{
	enum SortDirection { straight = 0, left = 1, right = 2 }

	[SerializeField] GameObject _leftCollider, _rightCollider, _centerColliders;
	[SerializeField] SorterFilterBasket _filterLeft, _filterRight;

	Collider[] leftCols, rightCols, centerCols;
	readonly Dictionary<Component, SortDirection> directionByOre = new Dictionary<Component, SortDirection>();
	readonly Dictionary<Component, HashSet<Component>> ignoredWith = new Dictionary<Component, HashSet<Component>>();
	readonly Dictionary<Component, Collider[]> collidersByOre = new Dictionary<Component, Collider[]>();

	void Awake()
	{
		leftCols = _leftCollider.GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>();
		rightCols = _rightCollider.GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>();
		centerCols = _centerColliders.GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>();
	}

	void OnEnable() => StartCoroutine(WaitThenReSortOre());

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessIdentity identity = other.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
		if (identity != null) SortOre(identity as Component, identity);
		else SetCollisions(other.gameObject, SortDirection.straight);
	}

	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		Component comp = other.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>() as Component;
		if (comp == null) return;
		if (ignoredWith.TryGetValue(comp, out var set))
			foreach (var other2 in new List<Component>(set)) IgnoreOrePair(comp, other2, false);
		ignoredWith.Remove(comp); directionByOre.Remove(comp); collidersByOre.Remove(comp);
	}

	/// <summary> Determines lane and sets collisions for this ore piece. </summary>
	void SortOre(Component comp, IProcessIdentity identity)
	{
		if (directionByOre.ContainsKey(comp)) return;
		bool matchL = _filterLeft.OreMatchesFilter(identity), matchR = _filterRight.OreMatchesFilter(identity);
		if (matchL && matchR) SetOreCollisions(comp, (SortDirection)Random.Range(1, 3));
		else if (matchL) SetOreCollisions(comp, SortDirection.left);
		else if (matchR) SetOreCollisions(comp, SortDirection.right);
		else SetOreCollisions(comp, SortDirection.straight);
	}

	void SetOreCollisions(Component comp, SortDirection dir)
	{
		directionByOre[comp] = dir;
		if (!ignoredWith.ContainsKey(comp)) ignoredWith[comp] = new HashSet<Component>();
		if (!collidersByOre.ContainsKey(comp)) collidersByOre[comp] = comp.GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>();
		// → ignore collisions with ore going different directions
		foreach (var key in directionByOre.Keys)
			if (key != comp && directionByOre[key] != dir) IgnoreOrePair(comp, key, true);
		SetCollisions(comp.gameObject, dir);
	}

	void SetCollisions(GameObject obj, SortDirection dir)
	{
		Collider[] cols = obj.GetComponents<Collider>();
		switch (dir)
		{
			case SortDirection.straight:
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, centerCols, false);
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, leftCols, true);
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, rightCols, true);
				break;
			case SortDirection.left:
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, centerCols, true);
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, leftCols, false);
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, rightCols, true);
				break;
			case SortDirection.right:
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, centerCols, true);
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, leftCols, true);
				UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, rightCols, false);
				break;
		}
	}

	void IgnoreOrePair(Component a, Component b, bool ignore)
	{
		if (!collidersByOre.ContainsKey(b)) collidersByOre[b] = b.GetComponentsInChildren<Collider>();
		foreach (var ca in collidersByOre[a])
			foreach (var cb in collidersByOre[b])
				Physics.IgnoreCollision(ca, cb, ignore);
		if (ignore)
		{
			ignoredWith[a].Add(b);
			if (!ignoredWith.ContainsKey(b)) ignoredWith[b] = new HashSet<Component>();
			ignoredWith[b].Add(a);
		}
		else { ignoredWith[a].Remove(b); ignoredWith[b].Remove(a); }
	}

	/// <summary> Re-sorts all ore on enable (handles domain reload / building re-enable). </summary>
	IEnumerator WaitThenReSortOre()
	{
		yield return new WaitForFixedUpdate();
		if (gameObject == null || directionByOre.Count == 0) yield break;
		var comps = directionByOre.Keys.ToList();
		directionByOre.Clear();
		foreach (var comp in comps)
		{
			var identity = comp.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
			if (identity != null) SortOre(comp, identity);
		}
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/Dependency.md ==== -->
# SortingSystem — L2 ✅ Interface-Only (ZERO concrete imports)

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Phase | E |
| Level | **L2** (all interface deps — ZERO concrete) |
| Shape | 🔌 Adapter |
| Scripts | BaseBasket, SorterFilterBasket, SorterMachine, BulkSorter, Hopper, RollerSplitter |
| Owns Interface | **IHopperConvertible** |
| Imports Interface | IProcessIdentity + IBasketTrackable (OreSystem C), IMagnetGrabbable (ToolSystem B-1 — SorterMachine detach) |
| Concrete Deps | **NONE** |
| FREE | DataManager (light materials), UtilsPhaseB (IgnoreAllCollisions) |

## Architecture
6/6 scripts have ZERO concrete imports.
- **IBasketTrackable** (OreSystem C) → replaces `OrePiece.BasketsThisIsInside.Add/Remove(this)` bidirectional write
- **IProcessIdentity** (OreSystem C) → replaces `OrePiece.ResourceType` + `.PieceType` reads for filter criteria
- **IMagnetGrabbable** (ToolSystem B-1) → SorterMachine calls `ClearMagnetHolder()` before teleporting
- **IHopperConvertible** (owned) → Hopper calls on ChuteTop (Phase D implements) instead of concrete ChuteTop import
- **DataManager** → replaces `BuildingManager` for light materials (FREE infra)

## Internal Dependency Graph
```
  ┌── SortingSystem/ ───────────────────────────────────────
  │
  │  BaseBasket → trigger → tracks OrePiece list + BasketsThisIsInside
  │    └── SorterFilterBasket → builds (ResourceType, PieceType) filter criteria
  │  SorterMachine → queue + cooldown → OreMatchesFilter → teleport to Pass/Fail
  │  BulkSorter → 3-lane (Left/Right/Straight) via Physics.IgnoreCollision
  │  Hopper → OnEnable raycast down → ChuteTop.ConvertToHopperVersion
  │  RollerSplitter → round-robin alternating Left/Right via Physics.IgnoreCollision
  │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/Hopper.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: DataManager (FREE — raycast layer), IHopperConvertible (owned — SortingSystem). ZERO concrete ChuteTop import.

/// <summary>
/// I check for an IHopperConvertible building below me on enable. If found, I tell it to convert
/// to the hopper visual variant (wider opening). ChuteTop (Phase D) implements IHopperConvertible.
/// Raycasts down 1m on BuildingPlacementCollisionLayers.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as child of hopper building prefab.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Sorting/Hopper")]
public class Hopper : MonoBehaviour
{
	void OnEnable() => StartCoroutine(WaitThenCheckBelow());

	/// <summary> Waits one frame then raycasts down to find IHopperConvertible → ConvertToHopperVersion. </summary>
	IEnumerator WaitThenCheckBelow()
	{
		if (Singleton<DataManager>.Ins == null) yield break;
		yield return new WaitForEndOfFrame();
		if (!enabled) yield break;
		Vector3 origin = transform.position + Vector3.up * 2f;
		if (Physics.Raycast(origin, Vector3.down, out RaycastHit hit, 1f, Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.BuildingPlacementCollisionLayers))
		{
			IHopperConvertible conv = hit.collider.GetComponentInParent<IHopperConvertible>();
			if (conv != null) conv.ConvertToHopperVersion();
		}
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/Interface/IHopperConvertible.cs ==== -->
/// <summary>
/// Any building that can convert to a hopper visual variant when a Hopper is placed on top.
/// ChuteTop (Phase D) implements this. Hopper raycasts down and calls ConvertToHopperVersion()
/// via this interface — zero concrete ChuteTop import.
///
/// SortingSystem OWNS this interface (caller-defines / DIP pattern).
/// Implementors: ChuteTop (Phase D BuildingSystem).
/// Callers: Hopper (Phase E SortingSystem).
/// </summary>
public interface IHopperConvertible
{
    void ConvertToHopperVersion();
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/RollerSplitter.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: PhysicsUtils / UtilsPhaseB (FREE — IgnoreAllCollisions)

/// <summary>
/// I alternate ore between two output lanes: left and right. Each ore that enters trigger
/// goes straight (left colliders enabled, right ignored) or alternates (right enabled, left ignored).
/// Uses Physics.IgnoreCollision to steer. Simple round-robin — no filter logic.
/// Deduplicates with a small recent-objects queue (cleared every 3s).
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building. Single input conveyor splits into two output conveyors.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Sorting/RollerSplitter")]
public class RollerSplitter : MonoBehaviour
{
	[SerializeField] Collider[] _leftConveyors;
	[SerializeField] Collider[] _rightConveyors;

	bool nextGoStraight = true;
	readonly Queue<GameObject> recentObjects = new Queue<GameObject>();
	float timeSinceLastCleared;

	void Update() => timeSinceLastCleared += Time.deltaTime;

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		GameObject go = other.gameObject;
		// → deduplicate (same object re-entering within 3s)
		if (timeSinceLastCleared > 3f) { timeSinceLastCleared = 0f; recentObjects.Clear(); }
		else if (recentObjects.Contains(go)) return;
		recentObjects.Enqueue(go);
		if (recentObjects.Count > 10) recentObjects.Dequeue();
		// → alternate: straight or side
		SetCollisions(go, nextGoStraight);
		nextGoStraight = !nextGoStraight;
	}

	/// <summary> Enables one lane's colliders and ignores the other's for this object. </summary>
	void SetCollisions(GameObject obj, bool goStraight)
	{
		Collider[] cols = obj.GetComponents<Collider>();
		if (goStraight)
		{
			UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, _leftConveyors, false);
			UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, _rightConveyors, true);
		}
		else
		{
			UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, _leftConveyors, true);
			UtilsPhaseB.IgnoreAllCollisions(cols, _rightConveyors, false);
		}
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/SorterFilterBasket.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessIdentity + IBasketTrackable (OreSystem C — interface only), DataManager (FREE). ZERO concrete OrePiece import.

/// <summary>
/// I extend BaseBasket to build a filter criteria list from whatever ore is placed inside me.
/// SorterMachine checks OreMatchesFilter(IProcessIdentity) to decide pass/fail routing.
/// Drop ore in the basket → filter auto-updates. Light turns green (has filter) or red (empty).
/// Uses IProcessIdentity for ResourceType+PieceType reads, IBasketTrackable for bidirectional tracking.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as child of SorterMachine. Player drops sample ore into the basket.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Sorting/SorterFilterBasket")]
public class SorterFilterBasket : BaseBasket
{
	List<(ResourceType, PieceType)> filterCriteria = new List<(ResourceType, PieceType)>();
	[SerializeField] MeshRenderer _lightMeshRenderer;
	[SerializeField] int _lightMaterialIndex;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundDefinition _setFilterSound;

	/// <summary> Checks if a processable object matches the current filter criteria via IProcessIdentity. </summary>
	public bool OreMatchesFilter(IProcessIdentity identity) => filterCriteria.Contains((identity.GetResourceType(), identity.GetPieceType()));

	protected override void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IBasketTrackable trackable = other.GetComponentInParent<IBasketTrackable>();
		IProcessIdentity identity = other.GetComponentInParent<IProcessIdentity>();
		if (trackable != null && identity != null) AddToFilter(trackable, identity);
	}

	protected override void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		IBasketTrackable trackable = other.GetComponentInParent<IBasketTrackable>();
		if (trackable != null) RemoveFromFilter(trackable);
	}

	/// <summary> Adds ore to basket via IBasketTrackable + rebuilds filter from IProcessIdentity. </summary>
	void AddToFilter(IBasketTrackable trackable, IProcessIdentity identity)
	{
		if (!_basketOreList.Contains(trackable))
		{
			_basketOreList.Add(trackable);
			trackable.AddBasketRef(this);
			UpdateFilter();
		}
	}

	/// <summary> Removes ore from basket + rebuilds filter. </summary>
	void RemoveFromFilter(IBasketTrackable trackable)
	{
		_basketOreList.Remove(trackable);
		trackable.RemoveBasketRef(this);
		UpdateFilter();
	}

	void ChangeLightMaterial(Material mat)
	{
		var mats = _lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials;
		mats[_lightMaterialIndex] = mat;
		_lightMeshRenderer.sharedMaterials = mats;
	}

	protected override void OnDisable() { base.OnDisable(); filterCriteria.Clear(); }

	/// <summary> Rebuilds filter from all ore currently in basket via IProcessIdentity. Updates light color. </summary>
	void UpdateFilter()
	{
		filterCriteria.Clear();
		foreach (var trackable in _basketOreList)
		{
			var identity = (trackable as Component)?.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
			if (identity == null) continue;
			var entry = (identity.GetResourceType(), identity.GetPieceType());
			if (!filterCriteria.Contains(entry)) filterCriteria.Add(entry);
		}
		ChangeLightMaterial(filterCriteria.Count > 0 ? Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.GreenLightMaterial : Singleton<DataManager>.Ins.RedLightMaterial);
	}
}

<!-- ==== FILE: learn/phase-e/Scripts/_-Systems/SortingSystem/SorterMachine.cs ==== -->
using System.Collections.Generic;
using UnityEngine;

// deps: IProcessIdentity (OreSystem C — interface only), SorterFilterBasket (same system). ZERO concrete OrePiece import.

/// <summary>
/// I route ore to Pass or Fail output based on SorterFilterBasket criteria. Ore enters trigger →
/// queued → FixedUpdate processes one per cooldown (cooldown varies by PieceType). If ore matches
/// filter → teleport to PassTransform. Else → FailTransform. Large pieces (Plate, Rod, Pipe, etc.)
/// use *Large transforms. Detaches magnet before teleporting. MaintainObjectYValue preserves height.
///
/// Who uses me: placed as building. SorterFilterBasket is a child that defines what passes.
/// </summary>
[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Sorting/SorterMachine")]
public class SorterMachine : MonoBehaviour
{
	#region Inspector Fields
	[SerializeField] bool _maintainObjectYValue;
	[SerializeField] Transform _passTransform, _passTransformLarge;
	[SerializeField] Transform _failTransform, _failTransformLarge;
	[SerializeField] float _baseFlowRate = 2f;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] SoundDefinition _passthroughSound, _sortSound;
	// Phase H: [SerializeField] Transform _audioPosition;
	[SerializeField] SorterFilterBasket _filter;
	#endregion

	Queue<Collider> colliderQueue = new Queue<Collider>();
	float timeUntilCanSort;

	/// <summary> Processes one ore per cooldown from queue. </summary>
	void FixedUpdate()
	{
		timeUntilCanSort -= Time.fixedDeltaTime;
		if (colliderQueue.Count > 0 && timeUntilCanSort < 0)
		{
			IProcessIdentity ore = colliderQueue.Dequeue().GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
			if (ore != null) ProcessOre(ore);
			if (colliderQueue.Count > 0) timeUntilCanSort = GetCooldown(colliderQueue.Peek());
		}
	}

	void OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)
	{
		IProcessIdentity ore = other.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
		if (ore != null)
		{
			if (colliderQueue.Count == 0) timeUntilCanSort = GetCooldown(ore.GetPieceType());
			colliderQueue.Enqueue(other);
		}
	}

	void OnTriggerExit(Collider other)
	{
		if (other.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>() != null)
			colliderQueue = new Queue<Collider>(new List<Collider>(colliderQueue).FindAll(o => o != other));
	}

	/// <summary> Teleports ore to Pass or Fail transform based on filter match. Detaches magnet. </summary>
	void ProcessOre(IProcessIdentity ore)
	{
		if (ore == null) return;
		var comp = ore as Component;
		Rigidbody rb = comp?.GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
		// → physically detach from magnet (destroys SpringJoint + restores drag + re-enables collisions)
		comp?.GetComponent<IMagnetGrabbable>()?.DetachFromMagnet();
		if (rb != null) rb.interpolation = RigidbodyInterpolation.None;
		PieceType pt = ore.GetPieceType();
		bool isLarge = pt == PieceType.plate || pt == PieceType.rod
			|| pt == PieceType.pipe || pt == PieceType.gear
			|| pt == PieceType.geode || pt == PieceType.oreCluster;
		if (_filter.OreMatchesFilter(ore))
		{
			Vector3 pos = isLarge ? _passTransformLarge.position : _passTransform.position;
			if (_maintainObjectYValue && comp != null) pos.y = comp.transform.position.y;
			if (comp != null) comp.transform.position = pos;
			// Phase H: SoundManager.PlaySoundAtLocation(_passthroughSound, _audioPosition.position);
		}
		else
		{
			Vector3 pos = isLarge ? _failTransformLarge.position : _failTransform.position;
			if (_maintainObjectYValue && comp != null) pos.y = comp.transform.position.y;
			if (comp != null) comp.transform.position = pos;
			// Phase H: SoundManager.PlaySoundAtLocation(_sortSound, _audioPosition.position);
		}
	}

	float GetCooldown(Collider col)
	{
		IProcessIdentity ore = col.GetComponent<IProcessIdentity>();
		return ore != null ? GetCooldown(ore.GetPieceType()) : GetCooldown(PieceType.INVALID);
	}

	float GetCooldown(PieceType pt) => pt switch
	{
		PieceType.ore => 1f / _baseFlowRate,
		PieceType.crushed => 0.5f / _baseFlowRate,
		PieceType.ingot => 1.25f / _baseFlowRate,
		PieceType.gear => 1.25f / _baseFlowRate,
		PieceType.plate => 1.5f / _baseFlowRate,
		PieceType.pipe => 1.5f / _baseFlowRate,
		PieceType.rod => 1.5f / _baseFlowRate,
		PieceType.oreCluster => 1.5f / _baseFlowRate,
		_ => 1f / _baseFlowRate
	};
}

# Surfer — Critical Thoughts Log

> This file captures my critical thinking for each prompt — what I considered, why I made certain choices, and what I deliberately avoided. Appended with each new request.

---

## Prompt 1: "Analyse the entire source and provide detailed architecture documentation"

**What I thought:**

The `Scripts/` folder has ~130 subfolders but only `Assembly-CSharp/` (~200 files) is actual game code — the rest are Unity engine and third-party DLL decompilations. Focused there exclusively.

Read the largest/most connected files first (SavingLoadingManager at 853 lines, PlayerController at 888 lines) to map the dependency graph before reading leaf scripts.

The codebase uses Singletons everywhere — I considered whether to frame this as a flaw. Decided it's pragmatic for this scope and said so honestly rather than dogmatically criticizing it.

`FindObjectOfType` calls in runtime paths (BaseHeldTool.DropItem, etc.) are a genuine perf issue worth calling out. LINQ in hot paths (CastingFurnace) is another.

The PlayerController is a textbook God Object but splitting it would be a refactor suggestion, not a bug. Framed it as a learning opportunity.

---

## Prompt 2: "Create learn folder with the .md file"

**What I thought:**

- Straightforward file creation. Saved a memory so I always route future generated files to `learn/`.
- No architectural decisions needed.

---

## Prompt 3: "Build phase-a from scratch — interaction + shop cart system"

**What I thought:**

- Scoped to just 2 systems: world interaction (raycast + IInteractable) and shop/cart UI. Resisted adding inventory, save/load, or mining — those are future phases.
- Used Unity's built-in `UnityEngine.UI` (Text, Button, Image, InputField) instead of TextMeshPro to keep .NET 2.0 compatible and avoid extra dependency.
- Avoided `$""` string interpolation, `?.` null-conditional, `async/await`, and expression-bodied members for .NET 2.0 compat. Used `string.Format` and explicit null checks throughout.
- Created `GameEvents` as a static event bus rather than making every system subscribe to specific manager events — this is the right level of decoupling for this scope without introducing a full message broker.
- `ShopUI` passes `this` to `ShopItemButton.Initialize()` — I considered whether this is tight coupling. Decided it's acceptable because they're the same UI subsystem (parent-child). Decoupling this with events would be over-engineering.
- Made `ShopCategory` a ScriptableObject (original uses a plain `[Serializable]` class inside a list). ScriptableObject is cleaner for the editor workflow and more idiomatic for a learning project.
- `ShopItem` is a runtime class, not a ScriptableObject — correct, because it carries mutable state (lock, purchase count) that differs per session.
- Included `ShopSpawnPoint` with gizmo drawing — small touch but important for scene setup discoverability.
- The GUIDE.md is long but necessary. A from-scratch learner needs exact "create this GameObject, add this component, wire this field" instructions. Didn't shortcut it.

## Prompt 4: "Make sure no tight coupling — use events/GameEvents where needed"

**What I thought:**

- Audited all 17 scripts. Found exactly 2 real coupling issues:
  1. `ShopTerminal` directly reaching into `UIManager.ShopUI.gameObject.SetActive()` — crosses 2 system boundaries
  2. `SimplePlayerController` polling `UIManager.IsInAnyMenu()` every frame — unnecessary direct dependency
- Everything else is either read-only singleton queries (acceptable), same-subsystem references (necessary), or one-time setup reads (fine).
- Resisted the urge to event-ify `ShopUI → EconomyManager.AddMoney()`. That's a legitimate command — the shop *must* call the economy system to deduct money. Wrapping it in an event would add indirection with zero benefit.
- Resisted event-ifying `ShopItemButton → ShopUI` reference. They're parent-child UI components. Forcing them through GameEvents would make the code harder to follow for a learner.
- The `OnToggleShopRequested` event pattern is clean: ShopTerminal fires, ShopUI subscribes. Neither knows the other exists. If a second shop terminal existed, it'd work automatically.
- `OnMenuStateChanged` with cached `_anyMenuOpen` bool eliminates per-frame singleton access in the player controller. Simple, effective, no over-engineering.

## Prompt 8: "How does the main source handle lots of physics objects without slowing?"

**What I thought:**

- Three techniques, not one. Important to explain them as a coordinated system, not isolated tricks.
- **Object Pooling** (`OrePiecePoolManager`) is the biggest win — eliminates Instantiate/Destroy GC pressure. The composite key `(ResourceType, PieceType, IsPolished)` is clever because it avoids resetting mesh/material on reuse.
- **Self-regulating throttle** (`OreLimitManager`) is the most architecturally interesting. It only counts non-sleeping rigidbodies — this is the key insight. A pile of 500 ore sitting still costs nothing. Only moving objects matter.
- **Amortized cleanup** (`OreManager.Update` checking one ore per frame) is subtle but important. Prevents orphan accumulation without ever doing an O(N) scan in a single frame.
- The user asked "what technique" (singular) but the real answer is three techniques working in concert. Each alone isn't enough — pooling without throttling still crashes at high counts, throttling without pooling still gets GC spikes, cleanup without pooling still leaks.
- Didn't mention Rigidbody.Sleep() explicitly as a "technique" because Unity does that automatically — but it's critical context for understanding why OreLimitManager only counts non-sleeping bodies.

---

- The diff table (Section 12 in GUIDE.md) is the key deliverable. 10 rows covering every deviation: what original did, what we did, why. Plus a "What Stayed the Same" list proving we didn't change things unnecessarily.
- Updated the memory to capture all 5 rules: source fidelity, decoupling, Guide.md diff section, learn/phase-X folder, .NET 2.0 + summaries. This ensures consistency across all future phases.
- The diff section is educational — a learner sees both approaches side by side and understands the tradeoff. It's not just documentation; it's a teaching tool.

## Prompt 18: "OnEnable/Awake ordering conflict — how to handle event subscriptions?"

**What I thought:**

- The user identified a real Unity pitfall: `Awake()` and `OnEnable()` execution order across GameObjects is not guaranteed. If Script A subscribes to GameEvents in `OnEnable()` and the handler reads `Singleton<B>.Instance`, but B's `Awake()` hasn't run yet, you get a null ref.
- Established a clear lifecycle rule:
  - `Awake()` — singleton registration, `GetComponent` caching only
  - `Start()` — event subscriptions for permanent objects (all Awake done by now). Pair with `OnDestroy()`.
  - `OnEnable()/OnDisable()` — event subscriptions ONLY for toggled objects (UI panels). Pair together.
- Fixed `StartingElevator.cs` — moved `GameEvents.OnGamePaused` subscription from `OnEnable→Start` and unsub from `OnDisable→OnDestroy`. The elevator is never toggled, so it should use the permanent pattern.
- Checked all existing Phase A scripts: `ShopUI` correctly splits between `Start()` (toggle event — needs to hear it even when inactive) and `OnEnable()` (refresh events — only when visible). `SimplePlayerController` uses `Start()` — correct. `MoneyDisplay` uses `OnEnable/OnDisable` — acceptable since it's a UI element.
- This rule should be applied consistently in all future phases. Didn't save a memory for it because it's a standard Unity best practice, not a project-specific convention.

## Prompt 27: "What's the Fresnel highlighter? Isn't it just an outline?"

**What I thought:**

- Read `FresnelHighlighter.cs` (151 lines) and `HighlightStyle.cs` (50 lines) from the original source. It's NOT an outline — it's a Fresnel rim glow using a custom shader injected via CommandBuffer.
- Key distinction: outlines are geometric (inverted hull or edge detection), Fresnel is a dot-product effect on surface normals. Edges glow, flat faces stay transparent.
- The shader `Hidden/Focus/FresnelAdd` uses additive blending (One+One), no depth write, configurable ZTest for x-ray mode. 4 properties: _Color, _Power, _Intensity, _ZTest.

---

## Prompt 28: "What kind of shader does it use?"

**What I thought:**

- Found the compiled shader JSON at `Assets/Shader/Hidden_Focus_FresnelAdd.json`. Shader is baked (`m_ShaderIsBaked: true`), so actual HLSL isn't available — but all metadata is.
- Reconstructed the shader logic from properties, render state, and constant buffer layout. Fragment shader does `pow(1 - saturate(dot(V, N)), _Power) * _Color * _Intensity` blended additively.
- For Phase B, we need to write this shader from scratch (~20 lines ShaderLab) or use Highlight Plus instead.

## Prompts 30-50 (session): "Complete architecture redesign + hand-typing"

**What happened (summary of major decisions):**

### Architecture Redesign
- **PhaseALOG rewritten** — removed StringBuilder, uses `.ToNSJson(pretify: true)` from SPACE_UTIL. Per-collection targeting: `LIST_CATEGORY__TO__JSON()`, `DOC_CATEGORY_ITEM__TO__JSON()`, `LIST_CARTITEM__TO__JSON()`. All serialization lives in PhaseXLOG only.
- **Field_ prefix** — renamed ShopCategoryFields → Field_ShopCategory, etc. Convention: prefix = no logic. `SO_` = pure data, `Field_` = display only, `W` = session wrapper.
- **GameEvents.LogSubscriberCount** — every Raise method logs `[GameEvents] OnX raised → N subscriber(s)`. User renamed `Log` → `LogSubscribersCount`.
- **No defensive null checks** — let it crash, crash is traceable. Exception: `?.Invoke()` on events (can have zero subscribers).
- **Economy shortcut property** — `private EconomyManager Economy => Singleton<EconomyManager>.Ins;` No `?.` on core singletons — direct access.
- **`_` prefix only for [SerializeField]** — private non-serialized fields use camelCase.

### Folder Structure (final)
- **6 numbered folders:** `0-Core/`, `1-Managers/`, `2-Data/`, `3-MonoBehaviours/`, `4-Utils/`, `5-Tests/`
- **2-Data/ subfolders:** `SO_*` + `Field_*` (root), `Interface/`, `DataWrapper/`, `DataService/`, `Enum/`, `Entities/`
- **Key insight:** most of 2-Data/ is pure C# (testable via `new` instance). Only SO_ and Field_ have Unity dependency.
- **Orchestrator/** is the only special pattern in MonoBehaviours/ — wires Field_ instances. Everything else is just "MonoBehaviour with game logic."

### ShopUI Split into 4
- **ShopUI** (SubManager) → toggle + events + lifecycle ONLY. Zero business logic. ~40 lines.
- **ShopUIOrchestrator** → wires Field_ instances, AddListener, purchase flow, refresh. All UI logic here.
- **ShopDataService** → pure C# collection manager. Builds WShopItem wrappers, cart operations, snapshot. Includes CartItem as nested class. Merged cart service into data service (one service per domain).
- **UtilsPhaseA** → static helpers (TrySpawnAtShopPoint, formatMoney extension).

### UIManager Purpose
- Researched original UIManager.LateUpdate() — complex priority blocking (Q only opens quest if NOT in shop/pause/contracts).
- **Hybrid approach:** world-triggered opens via GameEvents (decoupled), keyboard routing + ESC close via UIManager (needs priority knowledge).
- UIManager justified by priority blocking — stays thin for Phase A, grows naturally when Q/Tab/ESC logic arrives in later phases.

### Unity Lifecycle
- **Self-init pattern:** SubManagers start ACTIVE, init in Start(), disable self. OnEnable = just announce "I'm open". Start runs once — never re-runs on re-enable.
- **Event-driven refresh:** removed RefreshAll() from Update(). Orchestrator subscribes to OnMoneyChanged + refreshes after every action. Zero polling.
- Added full Unity lifecycle order diagram to GOAL.md.

### Hand-Typed Audit (9/10)
- User hand-typed Phase A (19 scripts, shop system working). Audited all files.
- **What's great:** architecture solid, merged cart into DataService, W prefix for wrappers, DOC__ for dictionaries, ALL_CAPS for collections, #region blocks, .Ins instead of .Instance, SPACE_UTIL extensions (.map, .gc, .colorTag, .destroyLeaves, .toggle).
- **Minor issues:** moneyOrchestrator lowercase class name, lambda unsubscribe in ShopUI, DataService accesses Singleton directly, ShopSpawnPoint.GetRandomSpawnPoint not static.
- User's emphasis: **least possible public API + least possible private methods**.

### GOAL.md Final Version
- Complete rewrite incorporating user's actual coding style from hand-typed scripts.
- Core Principle: "Every script's purpose fits in one sentence. Every script performs ONLY that service — purely, nothing else."
- Added: Why This Structure (separation by responsibility not domain, natural MVP pattern).
- Added: comprehensive folder rules with one-liner purpose per folder/subfolder.
- Added: 14-question decision tree for file placement.

### PhaseMap.md Full Rewrite
- All 11 phases updated to new architecture: numbered folders, Script Purpose sections, folder-tree file lists, Vertical Slice Tests per phase, Modifications to Earlier Phases.
- Phase B: original PlayerController (888 lines) split into PlayerMovement + PlayerCamera + PlayerGrab + InventoryOrchestrator.

### New Files Created

- **Estimate.md:** ~153 hours total, ~7 weeks at 4hr/weekday + 8hr/weekend

### Key Rules Locked In

## Prompt 30+: "UIManager purpose, self-init pattern, Phase B complete build"

**What I thought:**

### UIManager Purpose
- User questioned: does UIManager need to exist if panels self-init?

## Prompt: "Build minemgl-graph.html — interactive dependency graph for all phases"

**What I thought:**
- User wants a comprehensive, interactive, standalone HTML tool that visualizes how every `.cs` file depends on every other across all 6 phases (All, A, A-1, B, C, D).
- **Read every single script** (~100 files) to extract actual dependencies — not inferred, not guessed. Every edge in the graph corresponds to a real code reference I verified.
- **9 edge types identified:** Inherits, Implements (interface), Get...() read, Set...() write, Event subscribe, Event raise, Singleton read, Creates/owns (new DataService()), Utils call. These cover every coupling pattern in the codebase.
- **D3.js force layout** was the right choice — nodes can be dragged, graph self-organizes, zoom/pan works naturally. Considered vis.js and cytoscape.js but D3 gives the most control over edge styling (dashed, dotted, colored arrows per type).
- **Claude AI theme:** dark background (#1a1a1a), JetBrains Mono (monospace), amber accent (#d97706), muted phase colors matching the legend. Not gaudy — functional and readable.
- **Interaction features:** phase toggles (hide/show entire phases), edge type toggles (show only inheritance, only events, etc.), search box with fuzzy matching + neighbor highlighting, click-to-inspect panel showing all incoming/outgoing dependencies with labels.
- **Node radius scales by connection count** — GameEvents, BaseHeldTool, PlayerMovement are visually larger because they have more connections. This immediately reveals hub nodes.
- **Curved edges (arc paths)** prevent overlapping parallel edges between the same pair of nodes (e.g., a script that both subscribes to AND raises events on GameEvents).
- **Tradeoff:** hardcoded node/link data vs dynamic parsing. Chose hardcoded because: (1) the scripts use SPACE_UTIL extensions and Unity APIs that a parser wouldn't understand, (2) I already read every file so the data is accurate, (3) a JS parser would be fragile and bloated.
- **Deliberate omissions:** didn't include handTyped(latest) folder separately — those are the same scripts the user is typing from the phase templates. Also didn't include test scripts' internal dependencies (they're leaf nodes).

## Prompt: "TODO.md bugs — tool pickup + drag-drop not working in Phase B"

**What I thought:**
- **Root cause of tool pickup failure:** HotBar was a CHILD of InventoryUI in the hand-typed scene. When InventoryUI self-disables (`SetActive(false)` in first OnEnable), ALL children including HotBar become invisible. The event subscription still fires, DataService adds the tool, but the Field_ slots are on disabled GOs → nothing visible. The generated GUIDE.md showed the correct sibling hierarchy but never explicitly warned "HotBar must NOT be a child."
- **Root cause of drag-drop failure:** Two issues: (1) DragGhostIcon's Image `raycastTarget` likely `true` → ghost steals pointer events from slots underneath → hover flickers, drop never reaches target slot. (2) `InventoryDataService.Swap()` swaps entire InventorySlot objects instead of just the `tool` field → after swap, `isHotBar` (derived from `index`) is wrong for both slots.
- **Created Proto_SlotDragDrop.cs** — standalone prototype that builds the entire UI from code at runtime. Only needs Canvas + EventSystem. Tests drag-drop, swap, add/select/equip/drop. If prototype works but real system doesn't → wiring bug confirmed. Explicitly sets `raycastTarget = false` on ghost and icons, `true` on slot backgrounds.
- **The guides were correct but not explicit enough.** The hierarchy diagrams showed sibling structure, but a beginner who sees "InventoryUI panel containing HotBar" in their mind naturally nests HotBar under InventoryUI. Needed a bold WARNING saying "if you put HotBar as child, it WILL break."

## Prompt: "Pitfall rules — 10 mandatory warnings for all Manual tests"

**What I thought:**
- **4 original pitfalls from Phase B bugs:** SetActive cascading, scene instance vs prefab, raycastTarget, swap contents. These were the bugs the user actually hit.
- **6 new pitfalls from Phase D audit:** Missing layers (silent -1 return), LayerMask fields at Nothing (raycasts return empty), cross-phase mods not applied (compile or runtime failure), dual collider setup (trigger + physical), static lists surviving domain reload, execution order attributes. These haven't been hit yet but WOULD cause the same "no error, just doesn't work" experience.
- **All 10 rules added to GOAL.md + NewAgent.md.** Each rule says: what goes wrong, why it's silent, what the Manual test must include. The agent checks every Manual/*.md against these 10 rules before delivery.
- **Phase D Manual tests updated:** BuildingPlacementTest.md got layer warning with "What Happens If Missing" table + LayerMask field configuration list + cross-phase prerequisites + static list warning. ConveyorFlowTest.md got BasePhysicsObject stub warning + dual collider warning + execution order warning. ScaffoldingTest.md got LayerMask + prefab assignment warnings. GUIDE.md got top-of-file ⚠️ warning box.
- **Prototype convention documented:** `learn/prototype/` — one .cs = one mechanic, zero dependencies. User decides which prototypes are needed.

## Prompt: "Phase B System Architecture Overhaul — _-Systems/, IInventoryItem, Portability"

**End Goal:** Match main-source behavior with clean architecture. Zero tight coupling between systems. Each system portable to future Unity projects where possible. Systems communicate ONLY via interfaces (IInventoryItem, IHighlightable) and GameEvents — never via direct class imports.

**What I thought:**

### Hybrid _-Systems/ Folder Structure
- **Old structure:** 9 inventory files scattered across 5 folders (2-Data/, 3-MonoBehaviours/Orchestrator/, 1-Managers/SubManagers/, 3-MonoBehaviours/UI/, 2-Data/Interface/). Impossible to see what belongs together.
- **New structure:** `_-Systems/FeatureName/` bundles tightly coupled files. Each system folder has code + test.md. Self-contained — read one folder, understand the whole feature.
- **Rule:** 3+ tightly coupled files → `_-Systems/`. 1-2 standalone files → domain folders. Shared infra stays layer-based (0-Core, 2-Data/Enums, 4-Utils).

### IInventoryItem — Full Decoupling
- **Problem:** InventoryOrchestrator had 3 direct `BaseHeldTool` references: `is BaseHeldTool tool` pattern cast for equip event, `is ToolBuilder` for button label, `BaseHeldTool active` for tool actions routing.
- **Solution:** Added `OnEquipped()`, `GetEquipButtonLabel()`, `HandleActiveInput()` to IInventoryItem. Each item handles its own equip/input/label behavior. Inventory system now has ZERO references to any tool class.
- **SetOwnerContext:** Added `SetOwnerContext(Camera, Transform, Transform)` to IInventoryItem. PlayerGrab sends camera+viewModelContainer+magnetPos to equipped items without knowing BaseHeldTool exists. Tool stores raw transforms — never knows PlayerMovement exists.
- **GameEvents:** Changed all events from `Action<BaseHeldTool>` to `Action<IInventoryItem>`: OnToolPickupRequested, OnItemPickedUp, OnItemDropped, OnItemEquipped.

### IHighlightable — Game-Agnostic
- **Problem:** `GetHighlightProfile(BaseHeldTool activeTool)` — highlight system needed to know about tools.
- **Interim fix:** Changed to `GetHighlightProfile(IInventoryItem activeItem)` — better but still coupled to inventory concept.
- **Final fix:** Removed parameter entirely → `GetHighlightProfile()`. Each object decides its own highlight logic internally. BuildingObject (Phase D) tracks active item itself via OnItemEquipped subscription. Highlight system is now 100% game-agnostic — drop into any Unity project with Highlight Plus and it works.

### ItemEquipBridge — Keeping PlayerSystem Portable
- **Problem:** PlayerGrab had ONE line that coupled it to IInventoryItem: `GameEvents.OnItemEquipped += (item) => item.SetOwnerContext(...)`.
- **Solution:** Extracted into 5-line `ItemEquipBridge.cs` in ToolSystem (not PlayerSystem). PlayerSystem is now 95% portable (only dependency: GameEvents.OnMenuStateChanged for grab blocking).
- **Pattern:** When you need to bridge two independent systems, create a tiny bridge script in the MORE SPECIFIC system (ToolSystem), not the generic one (PlayerSystem).

### Portability Scores (Final)
- **HighlightSystem: 95%** — 1 file, only needs Singleton base + OnMenuStateChanged
- **PlayerSystem: 95%** — FPS controller, grab, rope — zero game-specific refs
- **InventorySystem: 85%** — replace event bus + remove SPACE_UTIL → works in any game with UI slots
- **ToolSystem: 20%** — bridges every system, IS the game. Not designed to be portable.

### [AddComponentMenu] Convention
- All MonoBehaviours in multi-class files get `[AddComponentMenu("MineMGL/Category/ClassName")]`. This lets Unity's Add Component menu find them organized under `MineMGL/Tools/ToolPickaxe`, `MineMGL/Inventory/InventoryOrchestrator`, etc. — even though 8 tool classes live in one `Tools.cs` file.

### Decisions
- **Kept PlayerGrab.OnMenuStateChanged in PlayerSystem** — menu blocking is generic enough (any game has menus). Not worth extracting.
- **Kept Tool→Physics concrete dependency** — tools ARE physics objects (inheritance: BaseHeldTool → BaseSellableItem → BasePhysicsObject). Abstracting this would mean interface-wrapping every physics call — over-engineering.
- **Proto_InventoryFull proved the concept** before rewriting the real system. The prototype's stacking, equip toggle, scroll-skip-empty, and drag-drop patterns were copied directly into the real InventorySystem.
- **FLOW.md + GUIDE.md rewritten from scratch** — old versions had stale references to scattered file structure, BaseHeldTool coupling, and missing IInventoryItem architecture.

## Session: "Portable Systems + Phase A Decoupling + All-Phase Architecture" (Apr 27-30, 2026)

**What I thought:**

### Portable System Convention — "Copy Folder = Complete"
- Each portable system owns its interface inside the folder. `IShopMoney` in ShopUISystem, `IInventoryItem` in InventorySystem, `IInteractable` in InteractionSystem, `IHighlightable` in HighlightSystem, `IDamageable` in MiningSystem, `ISaveLoadable*` in SaveSystem.
- Initially put `IMoney` in `2-Data/Interface/` (neutral ground). User pushed back: "a portable system should come packed with everything." Moved to ShopUISystem. Correct — the interface belongs to whoever defines the contract.
- Renamed `IMoney` → `IShopMoney` for clarity (it's a shop-system contract, not a generic money interface).

### Bridge Pattern — Wiring Without Coupling
- **Bridge scripts live on the non-portable side** (the game-specific system). `ItemEquipBridge` in ToolSystem (not PlayerSystem). `MoneyBridge` in EconomySystem (not ShopUISystem).
- Bridges are for **runtime context** that the portable system needs but can't get itself (camera, ViewModelContainer, money provider). Static wiring (inspector refs) is for things that don't change.
- `MoneyBridge` fires `RaiseMoneyProviderReady(IShopMoney)` once on Start. `ItemEquipBridge` fires per-equip. Different timing, same pattern.
- Considered bridge for BuildingCrate→IInventoryItem (15+ methods to proxy). Rejected — over-engineering. BuildingSystem marked as game-specific instead. **Rule: bridges only for 1-3 method contracts, not 15+.**

### Game-Specific vs Portable — The Honest Classification
- Systems that **implement** another system's interface are game-specific (ToolSystem implements IInventoryItem, BuildingSystem implements IInventoryItem + IInteractable, EconomySystem implements IShopMoney).
- Systems that **define** an interface or communicate only via events are portable.
- Across ALL phases (A-I): **15 portable, 10 game-specific**. This is honest — not every system can be portable, and pretending otherwise with adapter bridges is worse.

### Inventory Bug Fixes (MockTool Testing)
- **OnEquipped timing bug:** Orchestrator calls `SetActive(true)` → `OnEnable` fires → `ownerViewModelContainer` is null → wrong model shown. Fixed: `OnEquipped()` re-parents AFTER `RaiseItemEquipped` delivers context.
- **Stacked drop:** Added `IInventoryItem.DropOneFromStack(Camera cam)` — items handle their own clone/crate logic. MockTool uses `Instantiate(gameObject)` + `DestroyImmediate(MockTool)` on clone (then changed to `cloneMock.enabled = false` to keep all components).
- **Drop position:** `_dropOffset = Vector3(right, down, forward)` — configurable per tool. Not dead-center.
- **Equipped item parents to ViewModelContainer** (child of Camera) — no LateUpdate needed, moves with camera automatically. Same as BaseHeldTool.
- **Collider disabled when equipped** (MockTool only — BaseHeldTool hides WorldModel which has the collider).
- **HandleItemPickup stacking into active slot** — was triggering toggle-off. Fixed: check `idx != activeBeforeAdd`, re-show equipped item if stacked into same slot.
- **Drag-drop 3D preview** — GO shows at full scale during drag outside UI, hides when back over UI. On release: enables physics + collider at preview position.
- `CanStack` + `TryMerge` for drag-drop merge between slots.

### Phase C/D/E/F/G/H/I Architecture
- All future phases mapped to `_-Systems/` in PhaseMap.md and StructureMap.md.
- New agent for each phase reads GOAL.md + NewAgent.md (phase-agnostic) + scans `Scripts/Assembly-CSharp/` for 100% coverage.
- PhaseMap/StructureMap structures are **target architecture** — the new agent fills in any missing files from deep source analysis.
- Phase B handTyped(latest) already restructured by user into `_-Systems/`. Phase A copied + decoupled (IMoney→IShopMoney, MoneyBridge).

### GOAL.md + NewAgent.md — Fully Updated
- Portability table: 25 systems across all phases with ✅/❌ + interface ownership + bridge placement.
- End goal stated explicitly: "100% main-source functionality with clever architecture — systems communicate via interfaces + GameEvents, making them portable to future Unity projects."
- NewAgent.md is phase-agnostic — just change target phase line, paste to new agent, go.
- All stale references cleaned: `GetHighlightProfile()` takes no params, EconomyManager removed from phase-All, `2-Data/Interface/` only for ISaveLoadableObject (not IInteractable), folder structure shows `_-Systems/` not old layer-based.
